From:           Patrick Kirkham

Hi Ron!

At last I got a a manual for my
HR.5 Printer. Thanks for the
reply to my June letter [about
excessive line feeds]. Enclosed
is a print-out before and after
[altering the printer's dip
switches]. [Still getting one
line feed too many - any help?]

The following is what I have set
up now: A Pye 16" colour tv, ZX
Spectrum 128K +2, a Hilderbay
printer interface,a HR5 printer,
2 microdrives.

About 3 weeks ago I got an "Echo
Soft Organ Master" from Omnidale
Ltd. Derby for `17.95 but the
tape has a fault - I'm waiting
for a replacement.

                    - Patrick

To Patrick Kirkham from Brian

If the linefeed problem is still
not completely resolved, look
again at my last reply in June's
OUTLETTERS as there were other
points I raised as well as that
of the printer dipswitches.

In addition, I'm puzzled as to
why you never told me you had to
customise and LOAD in some
special code for the Hilderbay
Interface in which you would
have had to specify the linefeed
code or did you buy your inter-
face 2nd-hand? Did it not occur
to you that it was relevant? If
you re-create the code you must
set the codes of carriage return
and linefeed at zero.

In the OUTLETTER after this one,
Allan Oxberry suggests a clever
alternative- change the linefeed
code to 0 in Tasword.To clarify:
select "g" at the menu. Graphic
characters are displayed. Just
press ENTER. "Reset Interface/
printer codes?" will be shown.
Press "Y". Just press ENTER for
all 4 control codes shown then
you'll see:
     Printer carriage return=13

Just press ENTER and you'll see:

     Printer linefeed=10

Type 0 and ENTER then just press
ENTER for the margins and try
printing. Follow this paragraph
OR the one before - NOT BOTH or
you may get NO linefeeds! -Brian

From: Allan Oxberry, GATESHEAD

Dear Ron and Brian,

The PATRICK KIRKHAM problem in
Issue 22 can be solved by going
to graphic mode and changing the
LINEFEED to '0' for I also had
this problem with my TANDY 105
using TASWORD 2 and doing this
fixed it.

My working conditions are a
Spectrum 48K,Interface 1 and one
drive and a Tandy DMP 105. The
Interface is new to the setup
for I used a WAFADRIVE before
this.

Now the problem I am writing to
ask your other readers is....

HOW can I get SCREEN dumps with
Interface 1 and my printer? It
works great printing text and
forms etc. but NO screens.

When I use the Wafadrive I can

I have tried codes and many art

             Yours hopefully,

                Allan Oxberry,

To Alan Oxberry from Brian

Try the print option in BUILDING
(Issue 22) or COSINFANTUTTI in
this issue. If you still can't
get a high-res screen dump it
would appear your printer does
not use Epson standard codes so
look in your printer manual and
let me know what codes your
printer needs to print graphics
(preferably send a photocopy of

if it's possible to adapt our
high-res dump.

However,if you DO get a high-res
dump from the above programs,
hang on a couple of months as
the COPY routine will appear in
OUTLET as a stand-alone utility.
                        - Brian

From: John Luby, DUNS.

Dear Ron & Brian,

Like just about everyone else
with Tasword 2, I've customised
the BASIC to include,among other
things,a CAT routine [see DRIVE-
CHAT this Issue for a Tasword 2
mods special - B.C.] In my case,
when LOAD, SAVE or ERASE is
chosen, I get an option to CAT
to screen or printer, or go
straight to the option.

I've been trying Tasword+2
lately. For some reason Tasword
128 didn't work very well on my
black plastic 128k, but the +2
version seems OK. The CAT option
is an absolute pain, however.

You can only switch it on or off
via the tedious Customise Prog-
ram option, and even then you're
stuck either with a CAT every
time or not at all. I'd rather
have been given the choice each
time LOAD, SAVE or ERASE was
called. There isn't room to do
much to the BASIC, so I tried
putting a simple CAT command
after the RANDOMIZE statement in
the first line. It worked OK,
but with no choice of drive, and
a simple INPUT for the drive
number was too much for the
memory. I finally managed by
reading the SCREEN$ at the point
on the main menu screen where it
displays the current drive
number. The first line of BASIC
now reads:

RANDOMIZE USR VAL"51968": LET d=
VAL SCREEN$ (VAL"21",VAL"29"): C
LS: CAT d: PAUSE NOT PI: RUN

Choosing the option B for BASIC
on the main menu now gets an
immediate CAT of the current
drive (to the screen only).
Another key press goes straight
back to the program. I can still
break out of the program with
BREAK, or by leaving the cart-
ridge out of the drive. The main
option for CAT is left switched
off permanently.

Keep up the good work.

John Luby.

Many thanks John   - Brian

From:            Malcolm Norwood
                 30 Elm Walk
                 Shephall

                 Hertfordshire



Dear Ron and Brian,


Whilst going over the back
issues you have sent me I have
certainly been struck by the
great variety of programs you
have covered, and by the great
strides you have taken in
quality and presentation since
the early days! Keep up the good
work both of you!

A few quick tips for Plus D (and
maybe Disciple) users. As well
as CAT 1 and CAT 1!, you can
also use CAT #3;1 or CAT #3; 1!
to obtain either the full or
abbreviated Catalogue listed to
the Line Printer. Another
variation is CAT 1;"filename".
This will give full details of
the file "filename" only. If you
have a number of files on a disc
with the same start or finish to
the filename (e.g. Outlet CODE
text files) then by the use of
the "Wildcard" characters (* and
?) it is possible to list only
these files. These points are
certainly not mentioned in my
Plus D handbook. I think I got
them from the Indug magazine
"Format".

A cry for help! I now have a
Centronics GLP printer. A useful
if rather pedestrian little
beast! Has anyone out there
managed to persuade Tasword 2 to
print a ` with one of these?

Tasman sent me an information
sheet which points to a char-
acter set in the code but chang-
ing the values of any of these
to anything seems to have no
effect whatsoever! Tasman say
that Tasword sends a 35 instead
of the Sinclair 'standard' code
of 96, but my GLP prints a '
which is the character for code
96! The correct code for a pound
sign on the GLP is 156 which is
not very 'standard' either is
it?

You may leave my address on any
part of this you decide to
publish so that anyone with any
ideas can contact me directly.

Much to my amazement the
OUTPRINT prog works beautifully
on my GLP even though it is not
Epson-compatible. I presume the
author avoided the use of ESC*
codes to make the prog. more
widely applicable? How are the
page breaks achieved? My printer
has DIP switch settings for 11
or 12 inch paper and of course I
am using 11.75 inch (A4) paper!
However if I change the DIP
switch the page breaks seem to
come in a different place,
though it still does not line up
with the perforations.

Does the prog. use the "Skip
perforation" command? If so is
it possible to change the number
of lines it skips? This may
enable me to get it nearer to
the perforations.

Well that's quite enough for
now. Funny how when you are  not
using  paper  and  pen   "verbal
diarrhoea"  seems  to  set   in!
Here's looking out for OUTLET 23
and keep 'em coming!

               Yours sincerely


               Malcolm Norwood.

To: Malcolm Norwood from Brian

Select "g" at the Tasword menu.
The graphics character will be
shown numbered 128 to 143. Enter
one of these that you do not use
for printing already. For
example, No.140 is the half
horizontal black bar graphic.
Next to it are listed 27 45 1.
These are the standard code for
underline. If you enter graphics
mode and enter this character
when you are typing some text in
Tasword then when you print it
the following text will be
underlined.If you use underline,
obviously use another graphic
character for the "`" sign. For
example, graphic 143 is the full
black square.This represents the


codes 27 112 49 which do nothing
on my printer at all! Suppose
you pick that one. Type 143 and
ENTER.The 143 will flash and the
INPUT prompt will be code? Type
156 and ENTER. Press ENTER again
to finish as you only need the
one code for your "`" sign. Then
press "n" against the "reset
interface/printer codes?" and
you're back at the menu.Whenever
you want a ` sign in the text
select graphics mode and type a
full black square graphic
instead. When you come to print
the text, this should print as a
"`" sign.It is possible to alter
the shape of the black square so
it looks like a "`" on-screen.
Let me know if you want to know
how to do this and I'll explain.

Alistair McColl has the same
problem using OUTPRINT with A4
paper (see last month's OUTLETT-
ERS). As mentioned there,I think
the pages are "calculated" for
length so it does not look hope-
ful for A4 use unless Mike Haine
can suggest a mod?...

                    - Brian

From:Bob Rutherford,BOSTON,LINCS

Dear Brian,

To start with I think you are
doing a splendid job and OUTLET
is a great help to people like
myself who know next to nothing
about programming etc. but how
the h*!* do you get 4 lines of
text (your OUTLET Back Issues
Sheet)? You have 4 columns all
running consecutively.

I have used OUTPRINT (3 columns)
but they run all over the place,
some on one page then another.
I have a 48K+, Plus D, Seikosha
SP-1200A1 (Epson-compatible). Is
there a printer code, e.g. TAB,
VERT, HORIZ, to make 4 columns?
                 - R. Rutherford

To Bob Rutherford from Brian

No, the BACK ISSUES sheets are
done "manually" by LPRINTING a
column in condensed mode,winding
the paper back to the top of the
sheet, re-setting the margin
further to the right and then
LPRINTing the next column!

If OUTPRINT is printing the text
correctly in sequence but over-
lapping onto the next page on
your set up you may be using
true A4 paper in which case the
only solution may be to use
normal printer paper.If the text
is NOT printing out in order
then we can only wait to see if
Mike Haine finds the answer.
                       - Brian

From: Chris Clayton, CARLISLE

Dear Ron & Brian,

I was puzzled by your request
for help with WordMaster as what
you ask about seems so simple.

Perhaps I have not properly
understood your problem, or it
occured to me that there might
be something wrong with your
program.

Anyway, here are the answers to
your questions:

1. You cat a cartridge from the
opening menu simply by pressing
"k". You change the drive number
by pressing "d".

2. You save files in two differ-
ent ways: (i) from within a file
by pressing "INV VIDEO" then "s"
and ENTER (you can rename file
first) (ii) from the opening
menu by pressind "s", inputting
name of file, then ENTER. BUT
this mode saves ALL the files in
memory together, under that
name. There is a special file
called "save!" which enables you
to select which of a number of
files in memory you wish to save
together ---very useful.


If this dosn't solve your
problem let me have more details
or I find Barry Parkinson of PCG
very helpful.

Next point: Machine Code is way
beyond me, but I would find it
helpful if someone could explain
simply what you have to do to
enter, save and use the M/C
listings in the variety of
different forms in which they
appear in magazines. (Or even an
offer to enter them for me from
some kind person?)

Very occasionally I find a list-
ing which could be useful, for
example there is one which my
son would like as it would
enable him to use his +3 disc
drive in 48k mode but it is in
mnemonics and I havn't a clue
what to do with it.
                  All the best,

                Chris. Clayton

To Chris Clayton from Brian


Thanks Chris. It seems to me now
that WORDMASTER doesn't like my
(Version 1) of Interface 1 as
pressing K will not CAT even on
the copy you loaned me. I won't
pursue this further but am just
"pleased" that I'm not going
crazy after all and there is a
rational explanation. Can you
just confirm next time you write
that graphics for "clip art" are
normal Spectrum SCREEN$ with
various images all over the
screen which WORDMASTER can
extract? If so, I can make up
some screens for OUTLET.

There are normally 3 forms of
m/code listings in magazines.

1.Mnemonics.These take the form:

         LD A,10
         PUSH AF    etc.

You need an assembler to enter
these in a similar way to typing
in a BASIC program. They are
preferable because you can edit,
alter and modify the program to
your heart's content and your
experience allows! You can also
spot obvious printing errors
whereas lists of numbers may be
anything. JACKSOFT (Issue 12) is
a complete assembler and an
improved version will appear in
a future issue of OUTLET.

2. Decimal values. These may be
simply listed with a BASIC
program to INPUT them or in
BASIC lines of DATA to be READ
into memory by BASIC. If I see
the former, I convert it to the
latter because you can easily
edit the DATA lines and check it
for errors whereas if you INPUT
values you can lose your place
or make an error and if you miss
a value then you cannot simply
POKE in the one you missed as
all the succeeding values will
be in the wrong addresses! You
may need to start all over again
or, at best, PEEK and POKE for
ages trying to sort it out.

3. Hex values. These are listed
in the same two ways as decimal
but INPUT is in two-character
strings thus...
                 3F  C9 etc

or the BASIC DATA is string DATA
e.g. "3FC94B002A"

Whereas the decimal values can
be POKED straight into memory in
sequence starting at the start
address shown, hex needs a
routine to convert it to decimal
first and either this routine is
included in the listing or it
appears elsewhere in the magaz-
ine or even an earlier issue.

The golden rule is ALWAYS SAVE
THE BASIC YOU HAVE TYPED IN
BEFORE RUNNING THE CODE!!

I've made a note to see if it's
feasible to write a program for
OUTLET - an intelligent, very
easy to use, hex or decimal
loader which can cope with all
the variations of listings and
give guidance to the user.

Meanwhile, I'd be very grateful
if you would send in a copy of
the listing you mentioned for a
routine to use the +3 drive from
48K!!! I'll type it in for you
and return the code and it may
be of great help for the coming
+3 version of OUTLET!

                      - Brian.

To Gerald Carter from Brian

Many printer infterfaces for the
Spectrum have two modes: one
"expands" the single code for
the keywords like PAPER, CLEAR,
PLOT etc so they print out in
full when you LLIST a BASIC
listing. The other mode just
sends the code as it is. To
clarify that: The code for the
keyword PEEK is 190, the code
for the letters P,E,E,K are 80,
69,69,75 and a 32 for the SPACE
before the next word. A printer
interface will, in "mode 1",
intercept the code 190 and,
instead, send 80,69,69,75,32 to
the printer so the word PEEK is
printed.In "mode 2" it will just
send the code 190.

In addition, "Mode 1" will
intercept any codes between 0
and 31 and NOT SEND THEM AT ALL.
This is because, in 48K BASIC,
there may be colour codes in the
BASIC listing itself which would
be interpreted in a different
way by the printer.For instance,
code 18 is used to show FLASH on
the screen listing but a printer
would regard it as meaning:-
"switch off condensed mode".

What if you really DO want to
"switch off condensed mode" or
send any of the dozens of
control codes to your printer
(including the graphics codes)?
You need to turn to "mode 2". If
you study your printer interface
instructions it should explain

how to do this(although it won't
use the expressions "mode 1" or
"mode 2" but may use "text mode"
or "expanded mode" or some other
expression). For example, with
the Kempston E Interface you use
the BASIC line COPY : REM CHR$ 0
and thereafter any code sent
through the interface to the
printer will go unchanged.

With Interface 1 one might use,
e.g. OPEN # 3;"T" which will
allow printing of the full
keywords or OPEN # 3;"B" lets
the codes go unchanged.


If you can find which BASIC
command "switches" YOUR inter-
face then try the following:-

Load COSINFANTUTTI from this
issue, BREAK and LIST 9782. Use
EDIT and enter the command to
turn "off" the keyword tokens
(i.e. permit all codes to be
printed) at the start of line
9782. Re-enter the line and RUN
the program. Wait until a design
has been drawn on screen and
then select USER'S OWN from the
printer options.

If you can't find the commands
and DATEL don't advise then send
me a copy of your interface
instructions and I'll see if I
can help you further.

Some databases SAVE the data as
separate data which has to be
re-LOADed into the database


program. That is, if you wish to
re-LOAD the data at a later date
you need to LOAD the original
program and then select LOAD
DATA or some similar prompt from
a menu. Other databases SAVE the
whole program including the data
and then you need to LOAD it
directly with LOAD "" without
using the original program at
all.Which type is your database?

When the database fails to re-
LOAD, whether you are re-loading
data into the original program
from an on-screen menu or
suchlike or whether you are
loading it as an independant
program, what error message do
you see at the bottom of the
screen? If it says "tape loading
error" then try SAVEing on a

different cassette and leave a
20 or 30 second gap at the
start.Try cleaning the tape head
with a commercial tape cleaning
kit. Are you sure you have the
mike lead connected properly
when SAVEing and the recorder
was recording? Can you SAVE any
other programs ok?

If, however, there is no error
message but the tape is ignored
when you try to re-load the data
then, either it has not been
SAVEd at all (see previous
paragraph), or it is a different
file type,e.g. you are trying to
LOAD it as an independant
program when it should be loaded
as CODE or DATA into the
original program or vice versa.

Ideally, of course, it would be
better if you can get it running
on microdrive but unfortunately
you don't say exactly what the
problem is. "still cannot get
the program to run" is too vague
for me to do other than guess!
Where the program tries to LOAD
from tape you must BREAK, note
the line number at the bottom of
the screen then EDIT and alter
the syntax from LOAD "NAME" to
LOAD *"M";1;"NAME" etc.

By the way, the MOVE code on the
original microdrive introductory
cartridge can MOVE any number of
files in sequence from tape.Just
use: *MOVE "C";;"" TO "M";1
although you may need to stop
the tape between files to give
time to SAVE to m/drive. - Brian.

To Patrick Kirkham from Brian

If the linefeed problem is still not completely resolved, look again at my last reply in June's OUTLETTERS as there were other points I raised as well as that of the printer dipswitches.

In addition, I'm puzzled as to why you never told me you had to customise and LOAD in some special code for the Hilderbay Interface in which you would have had to specify the linefeed code or did you buy your inter- face 2nd-hand? Printer linefeed=10

To Gerald Carter from Brian

Many printer infterfaces for the Spectrum have two modes: one "expands" the single code for the keywords like PAPER, CLEAR, PLOT etc so they print out in full when you LLIST a BASIC listing. The other mode just sends the code as it is. To clarify that: The code for the keyword PEEK is 190, the code for the letters P,E,E,K are 80, 69,69,75 and a 32 for the SPACE before the next word. A printer interface will, in "mode 1", intercept the code 190 and, instead, send 80,69,69,75,32 to the printer so the word PEEK is printed.In "mode 2" it will just send the code 190.

In addition, "Mode 1" will intercept any codes between 0 and 31 and NOT SEND THEM AT ALL. This is because, in 48K BASIC, there may be colour codes in the BASIC listing itself which would be interpreted in a different way by the printer.For instance, code 18 is used to show FLASH on the screen listing but a printer would regard it as meaning:- "switch off condensed mode".

What if you really DO want to "switch off condensed mode" or send any of the dozens of control codes to your printer (including the graphics codes)? You need to turn to "mode 2". If you study your printer interface instructions it should explain

how to do this(although it won't use the expressions "mode 1" or "mode 2" but may use "text mode" or "expanded mode" or some other expression). For example, with the Kempston E Interface you use the BASIC line COPY : REM CHR$ 0 and thereafter any code sent through the interface to the printer will go unchanged.

With Interface 1 one might use, e.g. OPEN # 3;"T" which will allow printing of the full keywords or OPEN # 3;"B" lets the codes go unchanged.

If you can find which BASIC command "switches" YOUR inter- face then try the following:-

Load COSINFANTUTTI from this issue, BREAK and LIST 9782. Use EDIT and enter the command to turn "off" the keyword tokens (i.e. permit all codes to be printed) at the start of line 9782. Re-enter the line and RUN the program. Wait until a design has been drawn on screen and then select USER'S OWN from the printer options.

If you can't find the commands and DATEL don't advise then send me a copy of your interface instructions and I'll see if I can help you further.

Some databases SAVE the data as separate data which has to be re-LOADed into the database

program. That is, if you wish to re-LOAD the data at a later date you need to LOAD the original program and then select LOAD DATA or some similar prompt from a menu. Other databases SAVE the whole program including the data and then you need to LOAD it directly with LOAD "" without using the original program at all.Which type is your database?

When the database fails to re- LOAD, whether you are re-loading data into the original program from an on-screen menu or suchlike or whether you are loading it as an independant program, what error message do you see at the bottom of the screen? If it says "tape loading error" then try SAVEing on a

different cassette and leave a 20 or 30 second gap at the start.Try cleaning the tape head with a commercial tape cleaning kit. Are you sure you have the mike lead connected properly when SAVEing and the recorder was recording? Can you SAVE any other programs ok?

If, however, there is no error message but the tape is ignored when you try to re-load the data then, either it has not been SAVEd at all (see previous paragraph), or it is a different file type,e.g. you are trying to LOAD it as an independant program when it should be loaded as CODE or DATA into the original program or vice versa.

Ideally, of course, it would be better if you can get it running on microdrive but unfortunately you don't say exactly what the problem is. "still cannot get the program to run" is too vague for me to do other than guess! Where the program tries to LOAD from tape you must BREAK, note the line number at the bottom of the screen then EDIT and alter the syntax from LOAD "NAME" to LOAD *"M";1;"NAME" etc.

By the way, the MOVE code on the original microdrive introductory cartridge can MOVE any number of files in sequence from tape.Just use: *MOVE "C";;"" TO "M";1 although you may need to stop the tape between files to give time to SAVE to m/drive. - Brian.

Обычно существует 3 формы листингов машинного кода в журналах:

1. Мнемоники. Они выглядят так:
```text
         LD A,10
         PUSH AF    и т.д.
```
Вам нужен ассемблер, чтобы вводить их подобно тому, как вы вводите программу на BASIC. Они предпочтительнее, потому что вы можете редактировать, изменять и модифицировать программу в свое удовольствие, насколько позволяет ваш опыт! Вы также можете заметить очевидные опечатки, тогда как списки чисел могут быть чем угодно. JACKSOFT (выпуск 12) — это полноценный ассемблер, и улучшенная версия появится в будущем выпуске OUTLET.

2. Десятичные значения. Они могут быть просто перечислены вместе с программой на BASIC для их ввода (INPUT) или в строках DATA на BASIC для их считывания (READ) в память. Если я вижу первое, я конвертирую его во второе, потому что вы можете легко редактировать строки DATA и проверять их на ошибки. А если вы вводите (INPUT) значения, вы можете потерять место или допустить ошибку, и если вы пропустите значение, то не сможете просто сделать POKE в пропущенное место, так как все последующие значения окажутся в неправильных адресах! Вам, возможно, придется начинать все сначала или, в лучшем случае, часами использовать PEEK и POKE, пытаясь разобраться.

3. Шестнадцатеричные (Hex) значения. Они перечисляются теми же двумя способами, что и десятичные, но INPUT выполняется в виде двухсимвольных строк, например:
